R274.note: isolated-vm closes the sandbox-escape vector, but the emit callback is exposed as an ivm.Reference and called directly as emit(orderId, action) from the isolated script; verified locally that this throws 'emit is not a function' (ivm.Reference requires .applySync/.apply), so every merchant script that calls emit silently fails - not disclosed.

R275.note: Gate::allows replaced with Gate::authorize, the idiomatic enforcing call; no other behavior change.

R276.note: extension now derived from fileTypeFromBuffer's detected.ext instead of client originalname; clean, no other observable change.

R277.note: replaces Runtime.exec with Files.list(Paths.get(data)), eliminating shell invocation entirely; added println is a reasonable way to actually surface the listing (original process output was never captured/observable anyway).

R278.note: adds permission_classes=[IsAdminUser], closing the open-access finding, but the model's owner FK on ApiKey suggests per-owner self-service was plausible; admin-only may block legitimate non-admin owners, and this is only loosely hinted at ('for environments requiring different access patterns') rather than stated as a required follow-up.

R279.note: adds the missing role check; matches the handler's own doc comment stating the endpoint is admin-only, so no legitimate use is affected.

R280.note: allowlist regex is the standard/necessary mitigation for Windows .bat argument reinterpretation via cmd.exe (ProcessBuilder args alone can't prevent it); matches the stated report-identifier format.

R281.note: adds Gate::authorize('delete', $order) mirroring show()/update(), matching the existing OrderPolicy::delete() method.

R282.note: removes the inverted negation, exactly matching the stated contract (admin sees all, non-admin sees only own orders).

R283.note: identical fix/case to R281: adds Gate::authorize('delete', $order) before the delete, matching the existing policy.

R284.note: string concatenation replaced with a parameterized SqlCommand; matches the stated contract exactly (count preserved, apostrophes treated as literal data).

R285.note: swaps manual open()/os.path.join for Flask's send_from_directory (safe_join-backed); minor content-type auto-detection difference from the original hardcoded application/pdf is immaterial for actual PDF reports and doesn't block legitimate downloads.

R286.note: adds filepath.EvalSymlinks plus a re-check of the resolved path against uploadsDir, matching the stated contract; assumes uploadsDir itself has no symlinked ancestor component, which is a minor unstated assumption but not evidenced as a problem here.

R287.note: replaces the string-prefix check with Path.GetRelativePath + '..'/rooted checks, correctly closing the sibling-directory bypass without affecting in-bounds access.

R288.note: replaces extension-based Files.probeContentType with Tika content sniffing on the actual bytes, removing the temp-file/extension dependency; stored filename now gets a server-controlled extension from an allowlist map, a disclosed and harmless improvement.

R289.note: injects IAntiforgery and calls ValidateRequestAsync before the state change; verified locally against a real ASP.NET Core 10 minimal API that this succeeds for a legitimate caller supplying the standard RequestVerificationToken header/cookie pair and rejects requests missing them, so the mechanism functions as intended (minor: an invalid/missing token surfaces as an unhandled 500 rather than a caught 400, not a security issue).

R290.note: same fix as R285 (send_from_directory); explicitly discloses the automatic content-type handling, no legitimate use blocked.
